I have been growing cotton on this same land for many years. My father grew it too, and my neighbors grow it. In Quzhou, cotton is what we do. This year will be no different.

My land is 2 mu. I will plant all of it in cotton, same as always. I cannot afford to experiment — I have three mouths to feed. I will use the improved seed variety I have been getting from the village supply station for the past several years. It performs well enough. I have no interest in the newer expensive hybrids the salesmen push.

Come April, after the soil warms, I will plough the field as I always do. I will apply base fertilizer before planting — urea, phosphate, and some potash. My neighbor uses a bit more nitrogen than me but I have seen his soil get tired, so I keep to what I know works on my land.

The well is mine and I control when I irrigate. I will water before planting to prepare the bed, then again at seedling stage, at flowering, and during boll setting. That is four or five times through the season depending on rain. This summer has been dry lately so probably five.

For insects — bollworm especially — I spray. Cotton without spraying is no cotton at all. I will spray maybe seven times, starting when I see the first signs. My eyes are not as sharp as they were but I know what to look for.

I expect around 250 jin of seed cotton per mu if the season is decent. That has been my usual.
